articles.headline: Haridwar faces 7,000-tonne waste pile-up after Kanwar Yatra
articles.summary: Following the conclusion of the Kanwar Yatra, Haridwar is struggling with over 7,000 tonnes of garbage accumulated in parking lots, camps, and Ganga ghats. The city administration, which usually handles 250 tonnes daily, has deployed 1,000 workers for a 15-day cleanup drive. Concerns have been raised regarding the impact on the local environment and water quality of the Ganga.

articles.headline: AAIB probe finds pilot took sleep medication before flight
articles.summary: An investigation by the Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau revealed that an Air India pilot, who lost altitude during a Delhi-Phuket flight, had taken sleep medication. The pilot claimed the medication was prescribed by a family doctor for insomnia. While a post-flight drug test was negative, the incident has sparked concerns over pilot health and airline safety protocols.

articles.headline: Maharashtra makes Marathi knowledge mandatory for commercial taxi licenses
articles.summary: The Maharashtra government has issued an order requiring all commercial vehicle drivers to have a working knowledge of the Marathi language. Starting August 18, applicants for taxi and auto-rickshaw licenses must pass a basic proficiency test. Failure to comply could lead to license suspension for up to three months. The move aims to ensure better communication between drivers and locals.

articles.headline: Landslide in Mumbai's Kurla tenements kills seven people
articles.summary: At least seven people, including four members of one family, were killed after a landslide triggered by heavy rains hit tenements in Mumbai's Kurla area. The landslide destroyed four homes and damaged several others. Municipal officials stated the incident occurred early Wednesday morning. Rescue operations were launched immediately, but the difficult terrain hampered efforts.

articles.headline: M.P. deploys armed guards to protect Chambal Wildlife Sanctuary
articles.summary: The Madhya Pradesh forest department will deploy over 100 armed guards and 35 CCTV cameras to protect the Chambal Wildlife Sanctuary from illegal sand mining. The sanctuary is home to critically endangered gharials and dolphins. This move follows a Supreme Court directive to intensify surveillance and set up permanent check posts in sensitive areas prone to poaching and illegal mining.

articles.headline: Govt directs ride-hailing apps to remove 'tip' prompts before rides
articles.summary: The Union Ministry of Road Transport and Highways has directed ride-hailing aggregators to stop inviting tips from passengers before a ride is completed. The directive aims to prevent discriminatory practices where drivers might choose passengers based on tip amounts. The ministry emphasized that any tip must be voluntary and only offered after the service is successfully rendered.

articles.headline: Karnataka CM Siddaramaiah allots portfolios to 15 new ministers
articles.summary: Karnataka Chief Minister Siddaramaiah has allocated portfolios to 15 newly inducted ministers. Key appointments include D.K. Shivakumar for Finance and Cabinet Affairs, and G. Parameshwara for Home Affairs. The expansion brings the cabinet strength to 34. The allocation follows weeks of deliberation between the Congress state leadership and the party's central high command in New Delhi.

articles.headline: Special court orders probe into Kharge trust land deal
articles.summary: A special court in Bengaluru has ordered a preliminary inquiry into alleged irregularities in the allotment of industrial land to a trust linked to Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge. The complaint alleges that the Siddhartha Vihar Trust was given preferential treatment in the allotment of a five-acre plot. The Lokayukta police have been directed to submit a report on the matter within a month.

articles.headline: Streaming apps found on Prajwal Revanna's phone in jail
articles.summary: Prison authorities in Bengaluru found a mobile phone with active streaming apps, including Netflix and Disney+ Hotstar, in the cell of former MP Prajwal Revanna. Revanna is currently in judicial custody facing charges of sexual abuse. A jail superintendent has been suspended, and a probe has been launched to determine how the prohibited device and internet access were smuggled into the facility.

articles.headline: Andhra CM Naidu warns of zero tolerance for digital offences
articles.summary: Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu has announced a zero-tolerance policy towards digital crimes, including online harassment and the spread of misinformation. Addressing police officials, he emphasized the need for a dedicated wing to tackle cyber-bullying and fake news. He warned that political affiliations would not shield individuals from legal action if they violate digital laws.

articles.headline: CAG report reveals SC/ST funds diverted for general category students
articles.summary: A report by the Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG) has revealed that funds earmarked for Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribe students were used for general category candidates in several central universities. The report highlighted a shortfall in financial assistance for reserved categories between 2020 and 2024. The CAG has recommended a strict audit of fund utilization in higher education institutions.

articles.headline: Supreme Court says GST arrest orders must include 'reasons to believe'
articles.summary: The Supreme Court has ruled that GST authorities must clearly communicate the 'reasons to believe' an offense was committed before making an arrest. The bench stated that withholding such reasons would deprive an accused of their right to seek legal protection. The judgment emphasized that the power to arrest is not an automatic consequence of an investigation and must be used judiciously.

articles.headline: China's first home-grown commercial jet C919 makes first international flight
articles.summary: The C919, China's first domestically produced narrow-body commercial jet, has completed its first international flight from Shanghai to Ulaanbaatar. Developed by the Commercial Aircraft Corporation of China (COMAC), the jet is positioned as a rival to Airbus and Boeing models. The successful flight marks a milestone in China's ambition to become a major player in the global aviation industry.

articles.headline: India on track to reach $1 trillion in exports by FY2027
articles.summary: Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal stated that India is on course to achieve $1 trillion in merchandise and services exports by the 2026-27 fiscal year. Despite global headwinds and geopolitical uncertainties, exports grew by 15% in the first quarter of the current year. The government is focusing on new trade agreements and boosting manufacturing in key sectors like electronics and green energy.

articles.headline: Ramesh Rangarajan appointed Chairman of Kasturi and Sons Ltd
articles.summary: Ramesh Rangarajan has been elected Chairman of Kasturi and Sons Ltd., the holding company of The Hindu Group. He succeeds the late S. Rangarajan and brings extensive experience in news media business and corporate governance. He also serves on the Boards of Kasturi & Sons subsidiaries and as an Independent Director on the Board of MRF Limited.

articles.headline: Tata Group governance and Trusts relationship under fresh scrutiny
articles.summary: The departure of N Chandrasekaran has raised questions about the balance of power between the Tata Sons board and the Tata Trusts. Experts highlight that while the board manages professional operations, the Trusts hold a 66% stake, leading to potential friction over long-term strategic direction and investment priorities. The next chairman will need to navigate this complex relationship.

articles.headline: Tata stocks lose ₹45,000 crore in market cap in one session
articles.summary: Shares of Tata Group companies faced heavy selling pressure following the news that N Chandrasekaran will not seek a third term. The group's combined market capitalization fell by approximately ₹45,000 crore on Wednesday. Major decliners included Tata Consultancy Services (down 3.71%), Tata Steel (down 1.57%), and Tata Motors (down 1.32%).

articles.headline: RBI unlikely to exempt Tata Sons from mandatory listing rules
articles.summary: Despite leadership changes, the Reserve Bank of India is unlikely to exempt Tata Sons from its mandate for 'upper-layer' NBFCs to list on stock exchanges. Tata Sons has been seeking de-registration as an NBFC to avoid listing, but regulatory experts believe the RBI prioritizes systemic importance and transparency over specific corporate leadership transitions.

articles.headline: Struggling BigBasket emerges as a key test for Tata Digital
articles.summary: BigBasket, a major unit under Tata Digital, faces significant pressure to show a path to profitability amidst rising competition from quick-commerce firms. The unit reported a consolidated loss of ₹4,974 crore in FY26, despite a 12% revenue increase. The incoming Tata Sons leadership will face the challenge of turning around this capital-intensive e-commerce venture.

articles.headline: Iran's military pivots to 'offensive' mode amid regional tensions
articles.summary: Iran is shifting its military posture from defensive to 'offensive,' according to recent statements from IRGC officials. The change includes new military appointments and a focus on long-range ballistic missile production. Officials stated that the military must be capable of taking operations into enemy territory if favorable conditions arise, amid ongoing tensions with Israel and the US.

articles.headline: SAT questions Zee's market ban logic, reserves interim order
articles.summary: The Securities Appellate Tribunal (SAT) has reserved its order on an interim plea by Zee Entertainment's Punit Goenka against a SEBI ban. The tribunal questioned SEBI's logic for a two-month market ban, noting that it could impact the company's share price and ongoing merger processes. SEBI had barred Goenka from holding key positions over alleged fund diversion.

articles.headline: RBI unveils draft directions on loan interest rate determination
articles.summary: The Reserve Bank of India has released draft directions requiring all lenders to have a comprehensive policy for determining interest rates on fixed and floating rate loans. The guidelines aim to ensure transparency and fairness in loan pricing. Lenders must review their interest rate methodology annually, including the benchmark used and the spread charged to different borrower categories.

articles.headline: India's exports rise 15% to $129 billion in April-July
articles.summary: Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal announced that India's merchandise exports grew by approximately 15% to $129.32 billion during the April-July period. Despite global economic uncertainties, the growth was supported by strong demand in sectors like engineering goods and petroleum products. The minister expressed confidence in reaching the $1 trillion export target for goods and services by 2026-27.

articles.headline: Fertilizer sales dip in July due to weak monsoon
articles.summary: Sales of key fertilizers, including Urea, DAP, and MOP, declined in July as a weak monsoon impacted kharif sowing across several states. Total sales fell to 191.44 lakh tonnes compared to 210.6 lakh tonnes in the previous year. Industry experts warn that lower fertilizer usage could lead to a drop in crop yields if sowing is not compensated for in the coming weeks.

articles.headline: Andhra Pradesh clears investment plans worth ₹2.08 lakh crore
articles.summary: The Andhra Pradesh State Investment Promotion Board (SIPB) has cleared 25 industrial investment projects totaling ₹2.08 lakh crore. Key projects include a ₹85,200 crore digital infrastructure plan by Renew AP Green Power and a ₹58,743 crore investment by Centre Holdings for data centres. These projects are expected to generate over 21,000 direct jobs across the state.

articles.headline: Meta Faces Lawsuits From 29 US States Over Child Addiction
articles.summary: Twenty-nine US states have sued Meta, alleging that Facebook and Instagram were deliberately designed to be addictive to children. The states are seeking age-based restrictions and an end to features like infinite scrolling to protect young users from potential psychological harm and behavioral health issues.

articles.headline: England Removes Team Curfew For Upcoming Pakistan Test Series
articles.summary: England captain Joe Root announced that players will have no team curfew during next week's Test series against Pakistan. The decision comes despite recent scrutiny surrounding the team's dressing room culture. Root expressed confidence in the players' ability to act responsibly without strict off-field restrictions.

articles.headline: Cambridge University Hires Academic Who Once Supported Terror Group
articles.summary: Cambridge University has appointed Farah Ahmed as an assistant research professor despite her past links to the proscribed Islamist group Hizb ut-Tahrir. Ahmed previously described Western education as a threat to Muslims and condemned democracy. The university defended the hire, citing its commitment to academic freedom and robust debate within the law.

articles.headline: Mass Theft Blights Mozart Anniversary Tribute In Salzburg
articles.summary: More than 200 gold-colored statuettes of Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart have been stolen from his hometown of Salzburg, Austria. The 50cm-high polymer figures, designed by artist Ottmar Horl, were part of a 320-piece public tribute for the composer’s 270th birthday. Officials suspect the disappearance of 210 statues was an organized theft.

articles.headline: Donald Trump Sued Over Paid Truth Social Access Scheme
articles.summary: Two US media groups have sued President Donald Trump for charging up to $100,000 per month for early access to his Truth Social posts. The lawsuit alleges the scheme is unconstitutional and corrupt, as early access to market-moving news regarding trade tariffs and war developments provides subscribers an unfair financial advantage.

articles.headline: US Senators Press For Faster Visas For Indian Students
articles.summary: Thirty US senators have written to Secretary of State Marco Rubio expressing concern over significant delays in student visa appointments. With the fall academic season approaching, the senators warned that a shortage of timely F, M, and J visa interviews at consulates in India and elsewhere could prevent students from starting their courses on time.

articles.headline: Iran Reorganizes Military Toward Offensive Doctrine For Regional Conflict
articles.summary: Tehran has shifted its military stance to an offensive doctrine, as signaled by top appointments by Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei. Officials stated the new approach aims to take operations into enemy territory, moving away from a primarily defensive posture as peace talks with the US remain stalled over the Strait of Hormuz.

articles.headline: Australia Revamps Media Laws To Force Tech Firm Payments
articles.summary: Australia will introduce laws requiring large tech firms like Meta and Google to strike payment deals with at least eight news outlets, up from six. The revamp aims to better support smaller and diverse media organizations. Digital platforms must pay a levy equal to 2.5% of their local advertising revenue to fund news content.

articles.headline: LS Panel Recommends Action Against Retired Justice Yashwant Varma
articles.summary: A Lok Sabha inquiry committee has recommended further legal action against retired Justice Yashwant Varma. The judge was indicted for failing to explain the presence of large sums of cash found at his official residence in March 2024. Despite his resignation from the Allahabad High Court, Parliament may still initiate removal proceedings.

articles.headline: Prajwal Revanna Found Using 5G Smartphone In High-Security Jail
articles.summary: A raid at Parappana Agrahara prison revealed that convicted former MP Prajwal Revanna was using a 5G smartphone loaded with social media and OTT apps. Despite signal jammers, the device had active connectivity via a SIM card from Andhra Pradesh. A prison official has been suspended for dereliction of duty following the discovery.

articles.headline: Bengaluru Woman Run Over By Mini Goods Vehicle On Slushy Road
articles.summary: A 32-year-old woman, Medha Akarsh, died after being thrown into the path of a mini goods vehicle in Electronics City. The scooter she was riding pillion on skidded during sudden braking on a damaged, slushy stretch of road. Residents have blamed civic neglect and the poor condition of Anantnagar Main Road for the fatal mishap.

articles.headline: Government Warns Air India Over Safety And Pilot Drug Testing
articles.summary: The aviation ministry has warned Air India to improve operational oversight following a Phuket-Delhi flight incident where the plane lost altitude. The pilot later tested positive for marijuana. The DGCA has been ordered to revise drug-testing rules, increase mandatory testing percentages, and enforce tougher penalties for personnel using narcotics.

articles.headline: SC Directs Maximum 15 UAPA Cases Per Special Court
articles.summary: The Supreme Court has directed that special courts trying UAPA cases should not be burdened with more than 12-15 cases at a time. The ruling aims to ensure speedier trials after the court found some accused languishing in jail for years while the prosecution cited hundreds of witnesses. The directive follows delays in a PFI activist's trial.

articles.headline: Food Safety Raids Lead To Closure Of Vidhana Soudha Canteen
articles.summary: Food safety officials raided canteens at Vidhana Soudha and Legislators' Home, sealing 'Mallige Ootada Mane' due to cockroach infestations and unhygienic conditions. Expired ingredients were found at various government-run eateries. The crackdown aims to enforce FSSAI standards across public and private hostels and canteens in Bengaluru.

articles.headline: Tejasvi Surya Seeks Technical Review Of Proposed Hebbal Tunnel
articles.summary: Bengaluru South MP Tejasvi Surya has requested an independent technical review of the Rs 1,139 crore Hebbal short tunnel project. Surya cited concerns over safety, traffic simulation, and the impact on Hebbal Lake. He urged the government to consult experts from IISc and DULT before proceeding with construction of the three-lane tunnel.

articles.headline: Eight Year Old Bengaluru Boy Scales Africa's Highest Peak
articles.summary: Samarth Disan, an eight-year-old from Bengaluru, successfully summited Mount Kilimanjaro in Tanzania. Accompanied by his 11-year-old brother Sahas and their parents, Samarth completed the seven-day trek through diverse terrains. He is among the youngest Indians to reach the 5,895-metre peak, following months of preparation and strength training.

articles.headline: 83 Lakh Karnataka Voters Risk Deletion From Draft Rolls
articles.summary: Over 83 lakh voters in Karnataka face the threat of deletion from the electoral draft list scheduled for publication on August 24. These voters are currently categorized as absent, shifted, dead, or duplicate. The Election Commission has extended the enumeration deadline to August 17 to allow booth-level officers to correct roll details.

articles.headline: 300 Electric Two Wheelers Destroyed In Bengaluru Parking Yard Fire
articles.summary: A massive fire at a parking yard in Ramamurthynagar gutted at least 300 electric two-wheelers. Preliminary investigations point to a battery explosion as the cause of the blaze. The vehicles were used on a rental basis by delivery agents. Police have booked the yard manager for negligence regarding hazardous parking conditions.

articles.headline: Sira To Bairenahalli Highway Expansion Project Gets Central Approval
articles.summary: The Centre has cleared the first phase of a major highway expansion in Tumakuru district. The Rs 1,585 crore project involves four-laning the 52-km stretch between Sira and Bairenahalli on NH-69. The upgrade is expected to reduce travel time to Tirupati and Chennai while providing a logistics boost to industrial areas like Vasanthanarasapura.

articles.headline: Seven Dead In Mumbai Landslide Following Heavy Rainfall
articles.summary: Seven people, including four members of one family, died when boulders and debris crushed homes in the Ashok Nagar area of Ghatkopar, Mumbai. The landslide occurred in a congested, vulnerable hillside location during the early hours of Wednesday. Rescue operations involving the NDRF were hampered by narrow lanes and continued rain.

articles.headline: Madhya Pradesh Bans Analogue Paneer To Protect Dairy Standards
articles.summary: Madhya Pradesh has banned the sale of 'analogue paneer,' joining Maharashtra and Gujarat in acting against dairy substitutes made with vegetable fats like palm oil. Chief Minister Mohan Yadav stated the state would focus on genuine dairy production. Authorities expressed concern that cheaper substitutes were being passed off as real paneer.

articles.headline: New Thin Film Material Increases Heat Sensor Sensitivity Hundredfold
articles.summary: Researchers at JNCASR in Bengaluru have developed a new thin-film material using scandium nitride that significantly improves heat detection. The material generates an electrical signal nearly 100 times higher than conventional theory predicts. The breakthrough could lead to more sensitive thermal imaging devices and efficient heat-to-electricity converters.

articles.headline: Hardik Pandya Stays At MI After Failed Gujarat Titans Move
articles.summary: Hardik Pandya’s attempts to return to Gujarat Titans failed after he insisted on being reinstated as captain. The franchise was unwilling to replace current captain Shubman Gill. Consequently, Pandya will remain with Mumbai Indians, despite a disappointing 2026 season and ongoing scrutiny regarding his fitness and leadership role.

articles.headline: Sabyasachi Mukherjee Announces Multi Year Partnership With The Met
articles.summary: Renowned Indian designer Sabyasachi Mukherjee is launching a multi-year collaboration with The Metropolitan Museum of Art in New York. The partnership will begin with a high jewelry collection at New York Fashion Week in September 2026. The designs will be inspired by 5,000 years of museum history, blending Indian craftsmanship with global heritage.

articles.headline: Cricketer Abhishek Porel Arrested In Kolkata On Assault Charges
articles.summary: Wicketkeeper-batter Abhishek Porel has been arrested by Kolkata police following sexual assault allegations by a medical student. The complainant alleged assault over three years under the promise of marriage. Porel, who plays for Delhi Capitals in the IPL, has denied the charges. The case has been registered under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita.

articles.headline: Campaigning Ends for Phase One of 2024 Lok Sabha Elections
articles.summary: Campaigning concluded for the first phase of the General Elections across 21 states and Union Territories. 102 constituencies go to polls on Friday. Key candidates include Nitin Gadkari and K. Annamalai. PM Modi and Rahul Gandhi held final rallies in various states. Issues like unemployment and inflation dominated the discourse as parties made their final pitch for the opening phase.

articles.headline: Nestlé Under Scrutiny for High Sugar in Infant Food in India
articles.summary: A report by Public Eye revealed that Nestlé’s infant cereal Cerelac contains added sugar in India, while being sugar-free in European markets like the UK and Germany. Experts warned this could contribute to childhood obesity. The FSSAI is reportedly examining the findings as the brand faces global scrutiny over health standards and discriminatory product formulations in developing nations.

articles.headline: Supreme Court Reserves Verdict on VVPAT Cross-Verification Petitions
articles.summary: The Supreme Court reserved its judgment on petitions seeking 100% cross-verification of VVPAT slips with EVM votes. The Election Commission argued that EVMs are tamper-proof and manual counting of all slips would delay results significantly. The bench noted the importance of voter confidence while questioning if the current system needs further procedural safeguards to ensure transparency.

articles.headline: Severe Heatwave Alerts Issued for Odisha and West Bengal
articles.summary: The IMD issued a severe heatwave alert for Odisha and West Bengal for the next three days, with temperatures expected to rise 4-6 degrees above normal. Authorities advised citizens to stay hydrated and avoid outdoor activity during peak hours. High humidity is expected to intensify the heat index, posing health risks to vulnerable populations across eastern India as summer conditions peak.

articles.headline: Row Erupts Over Doordarshan News Logo Changing to Orange Color
articles.summary: Prasar Bharati's decision to change the iconic Doordarshan logo color to orange sparked a political row. While the broadcaster termed it a vibrant aesthetic update, opposition leaders called it an attempt at saffronisation of public services. The change follows recent updates to the news set and branding aimed at modernizing the national channel's visual identity for a digital audience.

articles.headline: Mumbai Police Arrest Two Linked to Salman Khan Residence Firing
articles.summary: Mumbai Police arrested two suspects from Gujarat's Kutch for the firing incident outside actor Salman Khan’s residence. The duo, allegedly linked to the Lawrence Bishnoi gang, were caught via technical intelligence. A social media post from Anmol Bishnoi had earlier claimed responsibility, citing the actor’s past legal cases as motivation for the targeted intimidation and attack.

articles.headline: ISRO Outlines Two-Launch Plan for Chandrayaan-4 Lunar Sample Return
articles.summary: ISRO Chairman S. Somanath announced that the Chandrayaan-4 lunar sample return mission will require two separate launches using the LVM3 and PSLV rockets. The spacecraft components will be assembled in space before proceeding to the Moon. This complex docking maneuver is a first for India and serves as a stepping stone for the planned 2035 Indian Space Station and manned lunar missions.

articles.headline: Qatar Re-evaluates Mediator Role in Israel-Hamas Ceasefire Negotiations
articles.summary: Qatar’s Prime Minister announced the country is re-evaluating its role as a mediator in ceasefire talks, citing misuse of the mediation for narrow political gains. This comes amid stalled negotiations for a hostage release and humanitarian aid in Gaza. Tensions between Iran and Israel have further complicated regional diplomacy, threatening the stability of ongoing peace efforts.

articles.headline: G7 Ministers Discuss New Sanctions Against Iran Drone Program
articles.summary: Foreign ministers from G7 nations meeting in Italy are discussing new sanctions against Iran following its drone and missile strike on Israel. The focus is on disrupting Iran’s supply chain for military hardware. Leaders urged restraint from all parties to prevent a full-scale regional war, while Israel continues to weigh its strategic response to the unprecedented direct aerial attack.

articles.headline: IMF Upgrades India's GDP Growth Forecast to 6.8 Percent
articles.summary: The International Monetary Fund raised India’s GDP growth forecast for 2024-25 to 6.8%, up from its previous estimate of 6.5%. The upgrade reflects robust domestic demand and rising public investment in infrastructure. India continues to be the world’s fastest-growing major economy, according to the IMF’s latest World Economic Outlook report released in Washington this week.

articles.headline: Wipro Forecasts Muted Near Term Growth Amid IT Sector Slowdown
articles.summary: IT major Wipro reported a 7.8% year-on-year decline in consolidated net profit for the March quarter. The company forecast a cautious revenue outlook, citing a challenging macroeconomic environment and reduced discretionary spending by global clients. This follows the recent appointment of Srinivas Pallia as CEO, who is tasked with steering the firm through shifting market demands.

articles.headline: Ministry Approves Bengaluru-Pune Greenfield Expressway Project
articles.summary: The Ministry of Road Transport and Highways approved a new 700km greenfield expressway to reduce travel time between Bengaluru and Pune to seven hours. The project aims to improve logistics for industrial clusters in Karnataka and Maharashtra. Environmental assessments are underway for the high-speed corridor, which will bypass major city traffic to significantly improve freight movement.

articles.headline: Delhi Capitals Secure Dominant Victory Over Gujarat Titans in IPL
articles.summary: Delhi Capitals secured a dominant 6-wicket victory over Gujarat Titans after bowling them out for a mere 89 runs, their lowest ever IPL score. Mukesh Kumar took 3 wickets, while Rishabh Pant excelled with two catches and two stumpings. DC chased the target in just 8.5 overs, significantly boosting their net run rate in the points table as the tournament reaches its mid-way mark.

articles.headline: Centre moves Bill to bar states from taxing minerals
articles.summary: Union government introduces Bill to amend Mines and Minerals Act, 1957, prohibiting states from taxing minerals. This follows a 2024 Supreme Court ruling upholding states' right. The move aims to ease fiscal burden on the mining sector, which some states now see as a revenue stream, hurting manufacturers' competitiveness.

articles.headline: Chandrasekaran's exit sparks market rout for Tata Group stocks
articles.summary: N. Chandrasekaran's decision not to seek reappointment as Tata Sons chairman triggered a market rout for group stocks. His exit, following pressure from Tata Trusts led by Noel Tata over unlisted businesses' path to profit and potential IPO, signals a need for an orderly transition at the top.

articles.headline: Govt schools in states face shutdowns, low enrolment, poor facilities
articles.summary: An analysis reveals nearly 84,000 government and aided schools shut down, with 15 million fewer students since 2018-19. States like J&K, West Bengal, MP, UP, and Karnataka perform poorly on facilities. Cash transfers, driven by populism, are crowding out education spending, which falls short of Unesco's prescribed 15-20% of budgets.

articles.headline: Chandrasekaran's tenure: strong first half, challenges in second
articles.summary: Natarajan Chandrasekaran's nine-year term as Tata Sons chairman was a tale of two halves. The Tata Group delivered robust performance in his first term (FY17-FY22) with TCS, Tata Steel, and Tata Motors thriving. His second term (FY22-FY26) faced external challenges and underperformance from new private businesses.

articles.headline: PSU lenders hesitant on ECB due to shrinking cost advantage
articles.summary: Public sector non-banking financial companies (NBFCs) are reconsidering overseas borrowing (ECB) despite RBI's concessional hedging window. Rising US Treasury yields and increased dollar issuance by Indian banks have narrowed the cost gap with domestic bonds to 8-10 bps, making ECBs less attractive.

articles.headline: Big brands adopt 'city store' model in urban micro-markets
articles.summary: Major brands like Ben's Cookies and Ikea are opting for smaller "city stores" in urban micro-markets and residential lanes over single large destinations. This shift is driven by rising rents, dense catchments, and consumer preference for proximity, walkability, and repeat consumption over travelling for shopping.

articles.headline: Gold hallmarking to get 'sold' tag to curb theft
articles.summary: The Centre is planning a system to mark hallmarked gold jewellery as "sold" using its unique six-digit Hallmark Unique Identification (HUID) number after a transaction. This move aims to curb the sale of stolen or unauthorized gold items and prevent the reuse of HUIDs.

articles.headline: FCRA Bill referred to JPC amid opposition protests
articles.summary: The Lok Sabha passed a motion to refer the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment (FCRA) Bill, 2026, to a 31-member joint committee of Parliament for further scrutiny, amidst strong opposition protests and demands for its withdrawal.

articles.headline: RBI proposes internal caps on small loans, microfinance rates
articles.summary: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) proposed changes to interest rate calculations for banks and non-banks, suggesting lenders cap annual percentage rates for microfinance and small-value loans. The aim is to ensure that these loans are not usurious for borrowers.

articles.headline: India plans insurance reforms to curb healthcare costs
articles.summary: India is considering wide-ranging reforms of health insurance, including benchmarked treatment rates and a nationwide claims exchange. This aims to boost transparency in an effort to control some of Asia's highest medical inflation rates. Recommendations are expected by year-end.

articles.headline: FM Sitharaman advocates public capital as catalyst for private investment
articles.summary: Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman stated that public capital should serve as a catalyst for private investment rather than replace it. She outlined government measures aimed at making infrastructure projects more attractive to private investors, aligning with increased capital spending and disinvestment efforts.

articles.headline: India plans new strategic petroleum reserves at Bikaner, Bina
articles.summary: Amid energy-security concerns and the West Asia conflict, the Centre is planning two new Strategic Petroleum Reserves (SPRs) at Bikaner in Rajasthan and Bina in Madhya Pradesh. Feasibility studies are completed or underway for these sites, aiming to augment crude oil storage capacity.

articles.headline: HPCL, MRPL seek 6 million barrels of crude via spot tenders
articles.summary: State-run refiners Hindustan Petroleum Corp. and Mangalore Refinery and Petrochemicals Ltd are seeking up to a combined 6 million barrels of oil through spot tenders. HPCL plans to import 4 million barrels for September-October delivery, and MRPL up to 2 million barrels for 10-20 October.

articles.headline: RE-transmission gap poses key credit risk for renewable sector: Ind-Ra
articles.summary: India Ratings and Research (Ind-Ra) reports that the growing gap between renewable energy (RE) commissioning and transmission readiness is emerging as a key credit risk for the sector. About 84GW of the 196GW RE pipeline until FY32 faces delays in general network access operationalization.

articles.headline: Renewable developers can cut tariffs post-tender: MNRE
articles.summary: The ministry of new and renewable energy (MNRE) clarified that renewable energy developers can voluntarily cut tariffs after winning tenders, potentially clearing about 40GW of unsigned power purchase agreements (PPAs). This allows REIAs to accept lower tariffs without reopening original bids, making projects more acceptable to discoms.

articles.headline: Boldfit seeks $80-100 million from private equity funds
articles.summary: Bling Brands Pvt Ltd, operating D2C fitness brand Boldfit, is looking to raise $80-100 million from private equity funds, targeting a ₹3,000-4,000 crore valuation. The company, which designs and sells products across fitness and sports, nearly doubled its operating revenue to ₹139.7 crore in FY25.

articles.headline: Tiger Global exits TVF at cut valuation amid OTT slowdown
articles.summary: Private equity firm Tiger Global Management has fully exited The Viral Fever (TVF), selling its stake at a $22 million valuation—a quarter of its 2019 peak of $82 million. The exit comes as the OTT industry slows commissioning original content, affecting production houses like TVF.

articles.headline: Zetwerk eyes up to $400 million IPO by September
articles.summary: Zetwerk Pvt, an Indian contract manufacturer, is preparing to file for an initial public offering (IPO) that could raise as much as $400 million, targeting a launch as early as September. The Bengaluru-based firm makes industrial products for utilities, renewable energy, and AI infrastructure.

articles.headline: Vodafone Idea Q1 results signal potential turnaround
articles.summary: Vodafone Idea’s June-quarter (Q1FY27) results signal a potential turnaround, with the company adding 0.3 million subscribers—a first since the 2018 merger—and revenue growing 6% YoY to ₹11,689 crore. However, its ₹45,000 crore network investment plan still faces funding risks.

articles.headline: Coal India's SECL prepares for ₹10,000 crore IPO
articles.summary: South Eastern Coalfields Ltd (SECL), a subsidiary of Coal India Ltd, has initiated the process of appointing investment banks for an IPO expected to raise ₹8,000 crore to ₹10,000 crore. Coal India plans to divest up to 25% of its shareholding in SECL.

articles.headline: Manappuram Finance thrives on gold loans amid business shift
articles.summary: Manappuram Finance saw profitability pick up in Q1FY27, driven by robust gold loan growth, which contributed 82% to consolidated assets under management (AUM). The company is targeting 25-30% growth in gold loans in FY27, compensating for muted growth in other businesses amid asset quality concerns.

articles.headline: Zee seeks SAT permission to sell MF investments for operations
articles.summary: Zee Entertainment Enterprises Ltd asked the Securities Appellate Tribunal (SAT) to lift Sebi’s market-access ban, stating it needs to sell about ₹1,200 crore of liquid mutual fund investments to fund day-to-day operations. Sebi has opposed Zee’s plea, arguing serious violations by promoters.

articles.headline: PE firms broaden exit routes as IPO market slows
articles.summary: Private equity firms in India with mature assets are broadening their search for exit routes beyond the stock market. A soft initial public offering (IPO) run is prompting fund managers to explore secondary trades, sponsor-to-sponsor buyouts, and continuation vehicles to return capital to investors.

articles.headline: Chinese automakers' global expansion creates opportunities for Indian suppliers
articles.summary: India's largest auto parts maker, Samvardhana Motherson International Ltd (SAMIL), sees fresh growth opportunities as Chinese automakers like BYD Co. and SAIC Motor Corp. expand manufacturing globally. Indian suppliers with international footprints are well-positioned to support these companies setting up factories in Europe, South-East Asia, and Latin America.

articles.headline: Godrej Consumer board unaware of CEO Sitapati’s abrupt exit
articles.summary: Godrej Consumer Products Ltd (GCPL) chairperson Nisaba Godrej stated the board was unaware of CEO Sudhir Sitapati's abrupt exit plans, despite having granted him a fresh five-year term. Her candid comments hinted at underlying discord, while Sitapati cited his performance, leading to market uncertainty.

articles.headline: Government views Tata Sons chairman's exit as internal matter
articles.summary: The Centre is unlikely to intervene in the leadership turmoil at Tata Sons following N. Chandrasekaran's resignation, viewing the matter as an internal corporate issue to be resolved within the group. The government would consider stepping in only if formally requested by relevant stakeholders.

articles.headline: US revokes 13.4 million visas under Trump administration
articles.summary: Under President Donald Trump, the US state department revoked 13.4 million visas due to criminal activity, visa violations, and national security concerns, according to data.

articles.headline: Colombia’s coffee output falls following earthquake
articles.summary: Colombia's coffee output in 2025 is 175,000 60kg bags, as exports face a pause due to a devastating earthquake that blocked key supply routes.

articles.headline: Glenmark Pharma US subsidiary settles drug price-fixing for $15.3 mn
articles.summary: The US subsidiary of Glenmark Pharmaceuticals agreed to pay Humana Inc. $15.3 million to settle generic drug price-fixing and antitrust litigation allegations.

articles.headline: Ambani family India’s richest with ₹25.8 trillion wealth
articles.summary: Mukesh Ambani’s family remained India’s richest business family on the 2026 Barclays Hurun list with ₹25.8 trillion wealth, despite an 8.5% decline in fortune.

articles.headline: Aditya Birla Group to sell ₹1,909 crore UltraTech Cement stake
articles.summary: Aditya Birla Group’s Pilani Investment and Industries Corp. plans to raise as much as ₹1,909 crore ($200 million) by selling a 0.57% stake in UltraTech Cement Ltd through a block trade. The seller offers about 1.7 million shares at a 3% discount.

articles.headline: Iran plans to join New Development Bank soon
articles.summary: Iran will soon join the New Development Bank, the development lender established by the Brics group of nations, its central bank governor Abdolnaser Hemmati said. Iran joined Brics in 2024 and seeks alternative financial channels outside the dollar system amid US and international sanctions.

articles.headline: IEA projects larger global oil supply deficit amid Iran war
articles.summary: The International Energy Agency (IEA) predicts global oil inventories will tumble this quarter at more than twice the previous rate due to the Iran war, despite a deepening hit to demand from high prices. Oil markets face a 1.8 million barrels a day shortfall as hostilities undermine production recovery.

articles.headline: Grasim Industries returns to profit in Q1 on strong fibre business
articles.summary: Grasim Industries swung to a standalone net profit of ₹63.22 crore ($6.63 million) in the first quarter, compared with a net loss a year earlier. This turnaround was helped by strong earnings in its fibre business, which supplies materials for textiles, and narrower losses in its newer ventures.

articles.headline: Central Bank of India raises $250 million via FCNR-B window
articles.summary: State-owned lender Central Bank of India mobilized $250 million under the FCNR-B window introduced by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI), surpassing its July target. The bank aims to accumulate a total of $400 million by September end, the closure date for the special swap window.

articles.headline: Freelancers must build financial safety net and diversify income
articles.summary: Freelancers and gig workers need strong financial discipline due to irregular income and lack of traditional safety nets. Key strategies include diversifying income streams, stacking specialized skills, meticulous budgeting, maintaining emergency funds, and setting professional boundaries, as AI advancements pose new risks to single-skill demands.

articles.headline: Guide to establishing a family-funded NGO in India
articles.summary: To establish a charitable entity (NGO/foundation) in India, one must choose an appropriate legal structure: a public charitable trust, a Section 8 Company, or a charitable society. Considerations include control, liability, member count, and state. Compliance requirements, tax exemption (Income-tax Act, 2025), and FCRA (for non-citizens) are crucial.

articles.headline: Non-resident Indians can compare NRE Fixed Deposit rates
articles.summary: Non-resident Indians (NRIs) can open NRE fixed deposits with Indian banks, offering tax-free interest and full repatriability. These deposits can be managed online, and loans against them are available for various purposes, including to third parties, making them a flexible investment option.

articles.headline: Investments should provide freedom, not predict child's future
articles.summary: Parents should invest to give children financial freedom for diverse career choices, rather than funding predetermined paths. True wealth planning focuses on creating options for any future, acknowledging children's unpredictable interests and evolving job markets. This approach enables children to pursue passions based on conviction, free from financial pressure.

articles.headline: Do not hold onto losing stocks in your portfolio
articles.summary: Investors often hold onto losing stocks while selling winners, turning portfolios into graveyards of past bull markets. The golden rule is to sell anything you would not buy at today's price. Markets don't care about purchase price; ruthlessly purge underperforming stocks to improve financial health.

articles.headline: US yen intervention faces complications amid global economic shifts
articles.summary: The US Treasury's yen intervention, aimed at propping up the Japanese currency, temporarily worked but faces complications. Japan's rising debt service cost, political pressure on BoJ for low rates, and a muddled economic policy could lead to higher inflation, making the situation more complex and increasing asset volatility.

articles.headline: Four-step policy agenda to raise India’s credit rating
articles.summary: A four-step policy agenda is proposed to raise India's credit rating: lower the interest-to-revenue ratio by raising tax revenues, bring states fully into fiscal discipline, increase transparency of unseen liabilities (e.g., guarantees, municipal exposures), and move towards the 80% GDP debt anchor accepted by Parliament in 2017.

articles.headline: Democrats test strategies to win US battleground states
articles.summary: Democrats are testing centrist vs. progressive messaging in critical battleground states like Michigan, Pennsylvania, and Wisconsin, which are crucial for the 2028 presidential election. Outcomes of gubernatorial and Senate races will reveal which approach builds broader electoral coalitions in these demographically similar "Mi-Pa-Wi" states, which often vote together.

articles.headline: India’s diplomatic missions require strategic recast and diverse expertise
articles.summary: India's diplomatic missions need a strategic recast beyond traditional IFS career tracks, incorporating political envoys and domain specialists in technology, trade, finance, and defence. This fusion of political conviction, domain expertise, and world experience is crucial to maximize national advantage in complex global affairs, where economic, strategic, and institutional gains converge.

articles.headline: Yotta Data Services Plans 8,000 Crore IPO for AI Expansion
articles.summary: Hiranandani Group's Yotta Data Services is preparing to file for an initial public offering to raise between ₹6,000 crore and ₹8,000 crore. The funds will be utilized to expand data center capacity and invest in AI infrastructure, including GPU procurement. The company has appointed Kotak Mahindra Capital, ICICI Securities, and SBI Capital Markets as lead managers for the issue.

articles.headline: UN Report Mentions 2025 Red Fort Terror Attack Plot
articles.summary: A United Nations monitoring report states that Al-Qaeda in the Indian Subcontinent (AQIS) planned to attack the Red Fort in late 2025 and establish cells in Bangladesh. The report highlights the group's interest in developing chemical and biological weapons. Indian security agencies had previously investigated similar plots involving the use of toxic substances like ricin.

articles.headline: IT Sector Braces for Renewal of 13 Billion Dollar Contract Deals
articles.summary: Indian IT firms face a significant period of contract renewals, with deals worth $13.5 billion set to expire by December. Large clients are looking to consolidate vendors and leverage AI-led deflation to seek lower pricing. Approximately 800 deals are up for renewal, pressuring service providers to demonstrate productivity gains through automation to retain business.

articles.headline: JSW Energy Signs Pact for 920-MW Hydel Project in Bhutan
articles.summary: JSW Energy has signed an agreement with Bhutan's Druk Green Power Corporation to develop the 920-MW Kuri-Gongri Hydroelectric Project. The project is part of JSW's plan to reach 30 GW of generation capacity and 40 GWh of energy storage by 2030. The joint venture will follow a build-own-operate-transfer model, with JSW holding a 51% stake in the subsidiary company.

articles.headline: Government Intensifies Drug Quality Checks with 950 Actions Since 2022
articles.summary: Indian authorities have taken 950 enforcement actions against pharmaceutical manufacturers since 2022 to ensure drug quality. Measures include license cancellations, show-cause notices, and stop-production orders. The crackdown follows global concerns regarding the quality of exported Indian syrups. Over 1,100 cough syrup manufacturers have undergone intensive audits to meet standards.

articles.headline: Kia Gears Up to Boost India Production Capacity to Meet Demand
articles.summary: Kia India plans to expand its manufacturing capacity to meet rising domestic and export demand. The automaker recorded 17% sales growth in July, selling 191,949 vehicles in the first seven months of 2026. Kia is targeting annual sales of 410,000 units by 2030 and aims to introduce 10 new models, including electric vehicles, to capture a 7.6% share of the Indian car market.

articles.headline: Airtel Reworks Prepaid Portfolio to Lift ARPU Without Headline Price Hike
articles.summary: Bharti Airtel has discontinued several entry-level prepaid plans, including the ₹299 pack, in a bid to increase its Average Revenue Per User (ARPU). The move effectively nudges subscribers toward higher-value plans. Analysts expect this rationalization to lift Airtel's ARPU by 3-4% and improve overall margins without a direct headline tariff increase for the broader user base.

articles.headline: Gold Prices Surge 7 Percent in 10 Days Amid Festive Demand
articles.summary: Gold prices in India have surged 7% over the last 10 days, reaching approximately ₹1.52 lakh per 10 grams. The rally is driven by the upcoming festive season, including Raksha Bandhan, and firm global trends. Retailers report that despite high prices, consumer demand remains steady as buyers fear further price hikes. Silver has also seen a value-wise increase in retail interest.

articles.headline: Nirmala Sitharaman Calls on Multilateral Banks to Fund Private Infrastructure
articles.summary: Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman urged multilateral development banks to catalyze private investment in infrastructure at scale. Speaking at a BRICS event, she emphasized that public capital should act as a catalyst rather than a substitute for private funds. The minister highlighted the need for transparent project pipelines and credible long-term frameworks to attract investors.

articles.headline: Piyush Goyal Confident of Meeting 1-Trillion Dollar Export Target by 2027
articles.summary: Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal expressed confidence that India will achieve its target of $1 trillion in goods and services exports by 2027. Despite global uncertainties, India's exports grew by 15% in the first four months of the current fiscal year. Goyal noted that four new free trade agreements have opened significant opportunities for Indian industries in developed markets.

articles.headline: RBI Disclosure Tweak: Banks to Reveal Monthly Loan Rates
articles.summary: The Reserve Bank of India has proposed new norms requiring banks and NBFCs to disclose their internal benchmark lending rates on the first of every month. The move aims to increase transparency and allow borrowers to better compare loan products. Floating rate loans for individuals and MSMEs must be linked to an external benchmark, and banks must clarify all components of the interest rate.

articles.headline: No Progress in Iran-US Truce Talks Over Strait of Hormuz
articles.summary: Negotiations between the US and Iran for a truce in the Gulf have stalled, with no progress reported by mediators. Iran claimed its actions in the Strait of Hormuz are defensive, while the US has stepped up its rhetoric and military presence in the region. The deadlock has added to global energy supply concerns, as both nations refuse to back down from their established positions.

articles.headline: US Inflation Cools to 3.4 Percent in July as Fuel Prices Fall
articles.summary: United States consumer prices rose 3.4% in July from a year ago, showing a cooling trend as gasoline and energy prices declined. The data suggests that the Federal Reserve's interest rate hikes are successfully curbing inflation. Excluding volatile food and energy, core inflation rose 3.2%. Investors now anticipate that the Fed may begin cutting interest rates as early as September.

articles.headline: Astrotalk Joins Unicorn Club Following 100 Million Dollar ESOP Buyback
articles.summary: Spiritual-tech platform Astrotalk has achieved a $1 billion valuation after announcing a $100 million ESOP buyback for its employees. The startup reported a revenue of ₹1,176 crore for FY25 with a net profit of ₹32 crore. The buyback aims to reward long-term employees and consolidate the company's position as a leader in the global astrology and spiritual services market.

articles.headline: Yulu Raises 93 Million Dollars in Equity and Debt for EV Expansion
articles.summary: Electric mobility startup Yulu has raised $93 crore in a fresh funding round to quadrupled its fleet of electric bikes. The capital will be used to expand into new cities and enhance its battery-swapping infrastructure. The company aims to reach a fleet size of 200,000 vehicles by 2027, catering to the growing demand for sustainable last-mile delivery and personal mobility solutions.

articles.headline: Brics economies face constraints in mobilising private capital: FM
articles.summary: Union Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman stated that Brics nations encounter common structural challenges in mobilizing private capital at scale. She emphasized that public capital should catalyze, not substitute, private investment, and highlighted government reforms to facilitate private sector involvement in infrastructure.

articles.headline: Manappuram Finance names Ashish Singh as new CEO
articles.summary: Manappuram Finance appointed Ashish Singh as MD and CEO, effective January 1, 2027, succeeding V P Nandakumar, marking a transition to an institutionalized governance structure after Bain Capital's investment. Nandakumar will become non-executive chairperson.

articles.headline: Government considers MDR or tiered incentives to offset UPI costs
articles.summary: The Finance Ministry is exploring two options to address financial costs of UPI: reinstating Merchant Discount Rate (MDR) for high-value transactions/merchants, or a tiered incentive structure to reduce government support. Current budgetary allocation is ~2,000 crore vs. industry's ~20,700 crore operational cost.

articles.headline: Railways shifts six private rail line projects to HAM model
articles.summary: The Ministry of Railways has abandoned a revenue-sharing model for six new rail line projects totaling ~31,814 crore, opting instead for a de-risked Hybrid Annuity Model (HAM). Under HAM, the railways will bear traffic/tariff risks and provide 40% upfront grant, while private firms design, finance, and construct.

articles.headline: Tata group faces governance crossroads after chairman's exit
articles.summary: N Chandrasekaran's decision to step down highlights ongoing governance challenges within the Tata group. Experts emphasize the need to resolve friction between Tata Trusts (66% owner), Tata Sons' board, and professional management, crucial for leadership continuity and stability.

articles.headline: Tata Sons listing uncertainty persists; Chandra's pay grew faster than profits
articles.summary: Tata Sons' stock market listing remains uncertain as RBI reviews its NBFC de-registration, despite a past deadline. N Chandrasekaran's annual pay grew 14.1% CAGR (FY18-FY26), surpassing Tata Sons' consolidated adjusted net profit decline (-11.9%) and listed companies' profit growth (9.2%).

articles.headline: Governance disputes unfolded at Tata Trusts after Ratan Tata’s death
articles.summary: N Chandrasekaran's resignation caps nearly two years of upheaval at Tata Trusts following Ratan Tata's death in October 2024. Disputes arose over trustee appointments, Tata Trusts' oversight of Tata Sons, its private status, and the exit mechanism for the Shapoorji Pallonji group, leading to government intervention.

articles.headline: Tata Steel prioritized India expansion under N Chandrasekaran's leadership
articles.summary: Under N Chandrasekaran, Tata Steel focused on doubling Indian capacity through acquisitions and organic expansion, making India its 'primary cash engine.' European operations remain a 'work-in-progress' despite stemming losses, with plans for low-carbon steelmaking at Port Talbot to achieve sustainability.

articles.headline: Tata Digital's costly bets under scrutiny amid board concerns
articles.summary: N Chandrasekaran's tenure saw Tata group's foray into digital commerce and semiconductors, with substantial investments in Tata Digital (~26,000 crore) and Tata Electronics (~91,000 crore for a fab plant). Tata Digital reported a ~4,974 crore loss in FY26, raising board concerns over sustained funding for loss-making ventures.

articles.headline: Hindustan Aeronautics Q1FY27 net profit rises 15% to ~1,590 crore
articles.summary: Hindustan Aeronautics (HAL) reported a 15% year-on-year increase in net profit for Q1FY27, reaching ~1,590 crore.

articles.headline: Gujarat Fluorochemicals Q1FY27 net profit up 21% to ~221 crore
articles.summary: Gujarat Fluorochemicals reported a 21% year-on-year rise in net profit for Q1FY27, reaching ~221 crore.

articles.headline: Marksans Pharma Q1FY27 net profit nearly triples to ~157 crore
articles.summary: Marksans Pharma's net profit for Q1FY27 surged by approximately threefold year-on-year, reaching ~157 crore.

articles.headline: EID Parry India Q1FY27 net profit declines 43% to ~142 crore
articles.summary: EID Parry India reported a 43% year-on-year decrease in net profit for Q1FY27, falling to ~142 crore.

articles.headline: India's pharma exports grow 6.8% in Q1 FY27 to $8.10 billion
articles.summary: India's pharmaceutical exports increased by 6.8% year-on-year to $8.10 billion in Q1 FY27, driven by strong June shipments. This indicates sustained month-on-month momentum and global demand for Indian pharma products.

articles.headline: Reliance Brands partners to launch Fabletics activewear in India
articles.summary: Reliance Brands (RBL) signed an exclusive long-term partnership with Fabletics to launch the global activewear brand in India. It will debut online and with a mono-brand store at DLF Promenade, New Delhi, leveraging RBL's omnichannel model expertise.

articles.headline: Bharti Airtel discontinues popular prepaid plans, nudges customers to higher tariffs
articles.summary: Bharti Airtel has removed several popular prepaid tariff plans, including those with higher validity, as it aims to shift customers towards higher-priced plans and postpaid services. Headline tariffs remain unchanged despite the discontinuation of 1.5 GB and 2 GB daily data plans for 56/60 days.

articles.headline: D2C startups leverage quick commerce for festival product launches
articles.summary: D2C startups in food, beverages, and lifestyle are increasingly using quick commerce (qcom) platforms as launchpads for new products during the festival season. Companies like Zappfresh, Borécha, 1.5 Degree, and Gladful are introducing new items and expanding portfolios on platforms like Blinkit and Swiggy Instamart.

articles.headline: Google wearables to track insulin resistance, not glucose levels
articles.summary: Alphabet Inc.'s Google is introducing new health features for its wearables, including a tool to track insulin resistance over time. This tool monitors physiological factors indicating how hard the body works to produce energy from food, rather than continuously tracking glucose levels.

articles.headline: Ex-Alibaba AI architect Junyang Lin raises funds for AI agent startup
articles.summary: Junyang Lin, former Alibaba AI architect, has founded a startup to build AI agents, securing funding from Tencent Holdings and Chinese venture heavyweights HSG. His new firm aims to develop AI agents for both digital and physical worlds.

articles.headline: Half of India's GCC workers need reskilling due to AI: PwC-Ficci report
articles.summary: A PwC India-Ficci report indicates that nearly 46% of workers in India's Global Capability Centres (GCCs) will require significant upskilling or reskilling in the next three years due to AI's impact on job nature and required skills. 86% of GCC leaders expect substantial changes by 2030.

articles.headline: NaBFID plans to raise $3-4 billion via ECBs in FY27
articles.summary: The National Bank for Financing Infrastructure and Development (NaBFID) aims to raise $3-4 billion through external commercial borrowings (ECBs) in FY27, including a $500 million to $1 billion dollar bond issuance by September and a multilateral-guaranteed $1 billion loan.

articles.headline: Exim Bank forecasts 17.6% merchandise export growth in Q2FY27
articles.summary: State-owned Exim Bank projects India's merchandise exports to grow 17.6% year-on-year to $131.2 billion in Q2FY27, driven by geographical diversification, trade agreements, and buoyant demand in partner countries. Non-oil exports are expected to rise 20.3% to $113.8 billion.

articles.headline: Government offers Neet debate; Opposition remains unmoved
articles.summary: The government offered a two-day Lok Sabha debate on the Neet paper leaks, with Home Minister Amit Shah willing to reply, but the Opposition rejected the proposal. Parliamentary Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju suggested extending the Monsoon Session for discussion, but the Opposition insisted on accountability for pellet gun use against protesters.

articles.headline: India's private defense manufacturing at inflection point: Report
articles.summary: A quarter-century after reforms, India's private defense manufacturers reached nearly a quarter of national military production in FY26. Reports indicate investor interest, particularly in drones, electronics, and missile systems. Future growth relies on continued reforms, including faster acquisition timelines and shifts from platform to capability procurement.

articles.headline: India exports first gasoline cargo to Russia amid refinery disruptions
articles.summary: India has for the first time exported gasoline to Russia, with a 350,000-barrel shipment arriving in Moscow on August 5, and two more cargoes expected. This follows Ukrainian attacks disrupting Russian domestic refining capacity, leading Moscow to seek fuel from markets like India.

articles.headline: Over half of NCERT, 44% of CBSE posts vacant: Parliamentary panel
articles.summary: A parliamentary panel reports that over half of NCERT's sanctioned posts (1,596 of 2,844) and 44% of CBSE positions (933 of 2,117) are vacant. It warns that CBSE's reliance on temporary staff risks examination quality and recommends higher public spending on education to meet NEP 2020 targets and reduce high dropout rates.

articles.headline: RBI proposes external benchmark optional for NBFC loans
articles.summary: The RBI has proposed making external benchmark-linked loans optional for NBFCs, while mandating fair rates for small-ticket loans. It also aims for a harmonized interest-rate framework across regulated entities, ensuring rates are not usurious and all loans migrate to the new system by April 1, 2029.

articles.headline: SBI may tap overseas bond market again for liquidity
articles.summary: State Bank of India, having recently raised $500 million through a five-year US dollar bond, may seek further funds in the overseas bond market if additional liquidity is required. The recent issue was oversubscribed but the bank only raised $500 million despite a $2 billion order book.

articles.headline: CAG flags ~401 crore GST lapses in works contracts, revenue accepts findings
articles.summary: The CAG identified 1,334 cases of GST non-compliance in works contracts totaling ~401.42 crore, with the Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs accepting findings in 903 cases (~268.36 crore) and recovering ~15.88 crore. Problems included incorrect claims, short payments, and irregular ITC.

articles.headline: Andhra Pradesh exceeds job, SHG targets but lags rural housing
articles.summary: Andhra Pradesh surpassed its employment and self-help group (SHG) targets under the Twenty Point Programme in FY26, generating 185.9 million person-days of work and promoting 3,115 SHGs. However, it fell significantly short on rural housing (35% of target) and road construction.

articles.headline: US consumer inflation mild in July, Fed rate hike odds reduced
articles.summary: US consumer prices rose slightly in July, influenced by declining gasoline costs and benign underlying inflation, reducing the likelihood of an interest rate hike from the Federal Reserve next month. Despite the mild increase, inflation remains above the 2% target, keeping a rate hike later this year on the table.

articles.headline: US Senate bill seeks continued support for Tibet beyond Dalai Lama
articles.summary: A bipartisan US Senate bill, the 'Assuring the Future of Tibet Act' (AFTA), aims to ensure American support for Tibet beyond the 14th Dalai Lama's lifetime. It seeks to recognize the Central Tibetan Administration (CTA) as the legitimate representative and advocates for CTA observer status at the UN.

articles.headline: Assam floods recede after claiming 101 lives, causing widespread destruction
articles.summary: Floodwaters in Assam's Sivasagar district receded after an unprecedented crisis, leaving 101 dead and over 0.14 million displaced. Homes and crops were damaged, with over ~1,000 crore needed for repairs. Climate change, Brahmaputra's sediment load, and shifting channels contribute to 'compound flooding.'

articles.headline: Iran reports no progress on reviving Gulf peace deal with US
articles.summary: Iran states no progress has been made in talks to revive the interim Gulf peace deal with the US, following attacks on shipping and accusations of agreement violations. Iran claims the US reneged on commitments, including lifting blockades and releasing frozen assets.

articles.headline: OPEC lowers 2026 world oil demand growth forecast again
articles.summary: OPEC has lowered its forecast for world oil demand growth in 2026 to 580,000 barrels per day (bpd), marking the fourth consecutive downward revision. The producer group still expects a smaller impact on consumption than other forecasters, like the IEA, due to the Iran war.

articles.headline: Tencent reports 11% revenue growth, invests heavily in AI
articles.summary: Tencent Holdings' revenue grew 11% to 204.8 billion yuan ($30.4 billion), surpassing forecasts, enabling funding for its costly AI buildout. Capital expenditures soared over 65% to 52.8 billion yuan, reflecting significant investment in AI accelerators and memory chips.

articles.headline: Taiwan condemns planned China-Indonesia naval drills near its coast
articles.summary: Taiwan's government condemned planned Chinese navy drills with an Indonesian warship east of its coast, calling it a 'military provocation.' Taipei argues Beijing is trying to create a false impression of control over those waters, heightening regional tensions.

articles.headline: Embassy Office Parks Reit to join Nifty 500, Midcap 150
articles.summary: Embassy Office Parks Reit will be included in the Nifty 500, Nifty Midcap 150, and other NSE broad-based indices from September. This inclusion is seen as a significant step for India's listed Reit market, broadening investor access.

articles.headline: NDR Invit Trust files draft for ~750 crore public IPO
articles.summary: NDR Invit Trust, a privately listed infrastructure investment trust, filed a draft offer document for a ~750 crore public IPO. The offer includes a ~450 crore fresh issue and a ~300 crore offer for sale by Investcorp India Warehousing IFSC Trust.

articles.headline: Dhoot Transmission IPO oversubscribed 74.21 times on Day 3
articles.summary: Auto components maker Dhoot Transmission's initial public offering was oversubscribed 74.21 times on its third day, receiving bids for 1,85,19,71,585 shares against 2,49,56,363 on offer. QIBs bid 212.92 times, non-institutional investors 51.93 times, and retail investors 8.12 times.

articles.headline: Shiprocket IPO subscribed 97% on first day of share sale
articles.summary: Ecommerce enablement platform Shiprocket's initial public offering was subscribed 97% on its first day, with retail investors portion subscribed 3.33 times and non-institutional investors category 1.23 times.

articles.headline: Milky Mist Dairy Food IPO subscribed 2.17 times on Day 2
articles.summary: Packaged food company Milky Mist Dairy Food's ~1,553 crore initial share sale was subscribed 2.17 times on its second day of bidding. The IPO, closing August 13, has a price band of ~133-140 per share.

articles.headline: Mixed outlook for Tata group firms amid succession uncertainty
articles.summary: N Chandrasekaran's resignation creates near-term pressure on Tata group stocks, with analysts noting uncertainty around succession, capital allocation in new ventures, and strategic impact. While Titan and Trent show strong growth, TCS faces demand woes, and Tata Steel's India business remains resilient despite European losses.

articles.headline: Consumer focus boosted Tata group under N Chandrasekaran
articles.summary: N Chandrasekaran's chairmanship shifted Tata Sons towards a consumer-centric focus, marked by the formation of Tata Consumer Products Ltd (TCPL) through mergers and strategic acquisitions like Capital Foods and Organic India. Other consumer businesses like Trent and Titan also operate under this strategy.

articles.headline: TD Power Systems top gainer in A-group companies
articles.summary: TD Power Systems emerged as the top gainer among A-group companies on the BSE, closing at ~1,478.2, up 15.9% over the previous close of ~1,275.7.

articles.headline: TCPL Packaging trading volume surges 59 times average
articles.summary: TCPL Packaging witnessed a massive surge in trading volume, with transactions 59 times higher than its two-week average on the BSE. The stock closed at ~4,427.0, up 19.9% from its previous close of ~3,691.3.

articles.headline: Kerala stalling work at Mullaperiyar: T.N.
articles.summary: Tamil Nadu has informed the Supreme Court that Kerala's "obstructionist attitude" has stalled the implementation of a 2012 top court judgment allowing Tamil Nadu to raise the Mullaperiyar dam reservoir water level to 142 feet. Tamil Nadu cited Kerala's lack of cooperation in strengthening work.

articles.headline: NEET leak: court takes cognisance of chargesheet
articles.summary: A special fast-track court, adjudicating the NEET-UG 2026 paper leak case, took cognisance of the CBI's chargesheet against 13 accused. The court also sought responses from the accused on a CBI application for further investigation and will begin arguments on charge framing Thursday.

articles.headline: Uproar in RS over remark against CPI(M) lawmaker
articles.summary: The Rajya Sabha adjourned amid uproar after CPI(M) MP John Brittas alleged BJP MP Sushmita Dev called him 'lungiwala'. Opposition MPs protested at Makar Dwar, some wearing mundus to symbolize "unity in diversity."

articles.headline: Retail inflation hits 19-month high of 4.45% in July
articles.summary: India's retail inflation surged to a 19-month high of 4.45% in July, primarily driven by rising food and fuel prices. Food and beverages inflation quickened to 5.2%, while restaurant and accommodation services inflation hit 7.7%. Experts expect food inflation to rise further due to monsoon damage and global prices.

articles.headline: ‘Economic blockade’ in Assam hits life along border with Arunachal
articles.summary: An "economic blockade" in Assam's Dhemaji district, protesting an August 10 firing by Arunachal Pradesh-based miscreants, disrupted normal life along the disputed inter-State boundary. The Takam Mising Porin Kebang (TMPK) called the shutdown after 11 villagers were attacked in a land dispute.

articles.headline: IB staffer’s murder: HC seeks police’s reply on appeals by 2 convicts
articles.summary: The Delhi High Court asked city police to respond to appeals by two convicts in the murder case of IB staffer Ankit Sharma during the 2020 North-East Delhi riots. The court also issued notice on their plea seeking suspension of life imprisonment and listed the cases for December 2 hearing.

articles.headline: Refused venue for meeting due to ‘BJP pressure’: Dipke
articles.summary: Abhijeet Dipke, founder of the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), claimed their volunteers' meeting in Delhi's Naraina was cancelled after a banquet hall revoked booking due to "pressure" from the ruling BJP. He alleged similar refusals and intimidation against CJP meetings.

articles.headline: Shishtachar squads detain 1.05 lakh in over a year
articles.summary: Delhi Police’s Shishtachar squads have detained approximately 1.05 lakh people in 15,077 drives over a year for harassment, molestation, and other offences against women in public. Launched in March 2025, the initiative has seen 40,015 detentions this year, adding to the cumulative figure.

articles.headline: DMRC urges public to avoid flying kites near elevated metro lines ahead of I-Day
articles.summary: The DMRC issued an advisory urging the public to avoid flying kites near elevated metro lines ahead of Independence Day. Kite strings entangling with 25,000-volt Overhead Equipment (OHE) wires can disrupt services and be fatal. Delhi Police seized 1,398 reels of banned Chinese kite string.

articles.headline: AAP rattled by BJP govt.’s welfare schemes: Sood
articles.summary: Delhi BJP leader Ashish Sood dismissed AAP's allegations of irregularities in BJP government's welfare schemes as "baseless," claiming AAP is "rattled" by the schemes' launch. AAP countered, alleging inferior quality bicycles in the 'Vidya Vahini' scheme.

articles.headline: West Bengal teachers protest over stalled selection process
articles.summary: "Untainted" West Bengal teachers, who lost jobs in a recruitment scam, resumed protests after counselling for reappointment was indefinitely adjourned. This follows a fresh recruitment process ordered by the Supreme Court, leaving 15,403 teachers in limbo despite clearing exams again.

articles.headline: Congress, BJP workers clash as Minister joins sanitation workers’ stir in Alwar
articles.summary: Rajasthan Minister Sanjay Sharma's support for sanitation workers protesting outside the Municipal Corporation in Alwar led to clashes between BJP and Congress workers. The protest, seeking appointment letters for selected candidates, ended after five hours with some letters issued.

articles.headline: Anti-delimitation resolution is against T.N.’s interests, says BJP
articles.summary: BJP State president Nainar Nagenthran stated that the resolution passed by the TVK government in Tamil Nadu against the delimitation exercise was against the State's interests. He called it a political act affecting democracy, arguing constituencies should be based on population.

articles.headline: Ambedkar statues vandalised, replaced in Unnao, Etawah
articles.summary: Villages in Uttar Pradesh's Unnao and Etawah districts were tense after Ambedkar statues were vandalized. Dalits protested, demanding action, while the administration installed new statues. The Opposition Congress called it an "organised plan to humiliate the Dalit community."

articles.headline: Will have to see if there was split in Shiv Sena: SC
articles.summary: The Supreme Court stated it must first determine if there was a split in the Shiv Sena, as such a division may originate in the legislature party and percolate into the organisation and primary membership. The court is hearing pleas against the EC's order recognizing the Shinde-led faction.

articles.headline: Maharashtra makes Marathi proficiency mandatory for app-based cab drivers too
articles.summary: Maharashtra Transport Minister Pratap Sarnaik announced that functional Marathi proficiency will be mandatory for app-based cab drivers, extending a rule previously applied to commercial passenger vehicles. Aggregators like Ola, Uber, and Rapido will not be exempt.

articles.headline: West Bengal Assembly passes two Bills to increase Kolkata wards to 209, Howrah to 68
articles.summary: The West Bengal Assembly passed two Bills to increase the number of wards in Kolkata from 144 to 209 and in Howrah from 50 to 68. BJP MLAs questioned the criteria and voter distribution, while Minister Agnimitra Paul said it aims to improve civic services.

articles.headline: Faith healing poses challenge to authorities as diseases kill 7 tribal children in Madhya Pradesh
articles.summary: Seven children have died and 100 fallen ill in Madhya Pradesh’s Balaghat district from monsoon-related diseases among the Baiga tribe. Authorities face challenges due to remote accessibility and the community's reliance on ritualistic healing. Special health camps are now set up.

articles.headline: How sustainable is India’s E20 push?
articles.summary: India's E20 ethanol blending program, saving ₹2 lakh crore in foreign exchange, faces criticism for potential vehicle harm and forced implementation. While 2023+ vehicles are E20-engineered, legacy vehicles risk degradation and efficiency loss. Sustainability concerns exist if monsoon failures affect feedstock.

articles.headline: Supreme Court clarifies scope of police custody under BNSS
articles.summary: The Supreme Court clarified that Section 187(2) of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) enlarges the window for police custody, allowing it in parts for up to 15 days within the first 40 or 60 days of detention. This reverses the previous 15-day limit in the whole.

articles.headline: Amid tussle, NCSC panel to probe Centre’s de-reservation proposals
articles.summary: The National Commission for Scheduled Castes (NCSC) will "comprehensively review" all Centre's proposals to de-reserve Union government quota posts over the last three years. This follows a tussle and concerns that de-reservation proposals are often incomplete.

articles.headline: Justice Varma’s withdrawal from probe cannot end statutory inquiry, says panel
articles.summary: The three-member inquiry committee investigating former Justice Yashwant Varma stated his withdrawal from proceedings came too late and could not end the statutory inquiry. The panel rebutted Varma's allegations of procedural unfairness, concluding charges were "proved."

articles.headline: BJP leader slams visit by police officers to Jharkhand protest site
articles.summary: Jharkhand Assembly Leader of Opposition Babulal Marandi condemned a late-night visit by Ranchi's DC and SSP to a protest site where job aspirants were agitating over alleged recruitment exam irregularities. He demanded a CBI probe and slammed attempts to "forcibly remove" students.

articles.headline: Centre softens stance on FCRA Bill following several appeals
articles.summary: The Centre softened its stance on the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment Bill, 2026, referring it to a Joint Parliamentary Committee (JPC) after coordinated appeals from Christian organizations and a warning from a Trump ally. This move aims to break parliamentary deadlock.
