articles.headline: Opposition ‘fled’ from meaningful debate in Parliament: Nabin
articles.summary: BJP president Nitin Nabin accused the Congress and other Opposition parties of avoiding parliamentary debate and disrupting the Monsoon Session, claiming they were "neither serious nor earnest" about public issues. He alleged they fled from discussions to prevent their "lies" from being exposed.

articles.headline: CWC to hold meeting to chalk out strategy for various key issues
articles.summary: The Congress Working Committee (CWC) will meet on August 19 to finalize strategy on political issues, including student paper leak protests and alleged "theft" of Ram Temple donations. The meeting will also review party preparedness for early next year's Assembly elections.

articles.headline: Upper House passes Bills to change name of Kerala, strengthen NCDC
articles.summary: The Rajya Sabha passed the National Co-operative Development Corporation (Amendment) Bill, 2026, and the Kerala (Alteration of Name) Bill, 2026. The latter, aimed at changing the State's name to Keralam, aligns with the Union government’s commitment to removing symbols of slavery.

articles.headline: 7 dead, several injured in landslip after heavy rain lashes Mumbai
articles.summary: Seven people died and several were injured after a landslip struck Mumbai's Ghatkopar area in the early hours of Wednesday following heavy rain. Soil and debris collapsed onto houses in Gaushiya Chawl. Rescue operations are underway for one trapped person.

articles.headline: NIA arrests accused in Manipur IED attack case
articles.summary: The NIA arrested S. Palal Thadou in connection with an IED attack on a residential house in Manipur on April 7, which killed two children and injured one. Thadou allegedly handled finances for UKNA, a Kuki insurgent group not in peace talks.

articles.headline: Both demolition and rehabilitation duties of the govt., says SC
articles.summary: The Supreme Court backed an NGO's petition, emphasizing that demolition and rehabilitation are the government's "twin responsibilities" in a welfare democracy. Chief Justice Kant questioned states demolishing unauthorized structures without rehabilitation policies, noting residents often pay taxes and receive utilities for decades.

articles.headline: Final drug test results for flight captain awaited: govt.
articles.summary: The Ministry of Civil Aviation is awaiting final drug test results for the captain of an Air India flight that dropped 300 feet mid-air last week, injuring 24. The pilots were removed from flying duties pending inquiry, following reports of a positive marijuana test.

articles.headline: Nicobar project: tribal council says its concerns are being overlooked
articles.summary: The Tribal Council of Great and Little Nicobar accused the administration of overlooking its concerns regarding the Great Nicobar Island (GNI) development project. They claim officials want to force the Shompen, an isolated tribe, into a "modern lifestyle" and that their consent for wildlife reserves was ignored.

articles.headline: Panel asks govt. if it will push agenda for de-dollarisation
articles.summary: A Parliamentary Standing Committee on External Affairs questioned the government on whether it will push a "BRICS-led de-dollarisation agenda" at the upcoming 18th BRICS Summit. Members noted India's central bank's advocacy for linking BRICS digital currencies to reduce reliance on the U.S. dollar.

articles.headline: India’s first branded train set to run as ‘Sprite’ Tejas Express
articles.summary: India's first private train, the Lucknow-Delhi-Lucknow Tejas Express, launched by IRCTC, will now run as the 'Sprite' Tejas Express after IRCTC awarded advertising rights for six months. This marks the first time a train is named after a brand.

articles.headline: Big brokerages to show post CAS indicative close by August 14
articles.summary: Large brokerages, including ICICI Securities, Groww, and Angel One, will display indicative close prices on their websites and apps by August 14, following an uptick in the adoption of closing auction session (CAS), SEBI Chairperson Tuhin Kanta Pandey announced.

articles.headline: Govt looking at MDR charge to make UPI self-sustaining
articles.summary: The government is exploring two options to make the UPI platform financially self-sustaining: a charge on high-value transactions/merchants, or a tiered incentive structure to phase out government support. Current subsidies cover only 11% of the industry’s actual costs.

articles.headline: Germany is interested in buying green hydrogen from India, says Chargé D’ Affaires
articles.summary: Georg Enzweiler, Germany’s Chargé D’ Affaires in India, stated Germany is interested in buying green hydrogen from India and expanding renewable energy engagement. He sees India's "fantastic resources" for solar and wind energy, making it an attractive business model for energy exports.

articles.headline: PSBs’ bad loan write-offs shrink as recoveries rise
articles.summary: Bad loan write-offs by public sector banks (PSBs) have been declining annually, reaching ₹70,528 crore in FY2026, a 40% reduction from five years prior. Simultaneously, recoveries from these loans are steadily rising, indicating improving financial health for PSBs.

articles.headline: Repco Home Finance loan book grows 8.9% in Q1
articles.summary: Repco Home Finance reported an 8.9% year-on-year growth in its loan book to ₹15,990 crore as of June 30, 2026. Net profit for the first quarter of FY27 increased to ₹114 crore, with total income rising 6.1% to ₹468 crore.

articles.headline: Panel for private hospital FDI relook as it warns of rising healthcare costs
articles.summary: A Parliamentary committee recommended reviewing FDI limits for private hospitals, warning that aggressive corporatisation and foreign capital influx could escalate healthcare costs. It urged standardizing treatment costs, incentivizing private investment in tier-2/3 cities, and increasing reserved beds for economically weaker sections.

articles.headline: Marathoner-technocrat who gave new direction to Tatas
articles.summary: Natarajan Chandrasekaran, stepping down as Tata Sons chairman, is credited with giving new directions to the Tata Group, focusing on high technology, semiconductors, electronics, and battery gigafactories. The first non-Parsi to lead the group, he also expanded its aviation presence.

articles.headline: IPO-bound Milky Mist to grow without fresh debt
articles.summary: IPO-bound Milky Mist plans to expand into West and North India and build a new Maharashtra manufacturing unit, funding growth through "internal accruals" rather than fresh borrowings. The firm repaid ₹300 crore using pre-IPO funds and aims to repay another ₹500 crore from IPO proceeds.

articles.headline: N. Korea launches missile towards sea ahead of South Korea-U.S. drills
articles.summary: North Korea launched its second ballistic missile in less than a week towards the sea on Wednesday, ahead of upcoming South Korea-U.S. military drills. South Korea's military remains ready to repel any provocation.

articles.headline: Paramilitary force launches drone attacks across Sudan
articles.summary: Sudan’s paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF) launched drone strikes on the capital Khartoum and other army-controlled cities on Wednesday. An RSF spokesperson confirmed targets included the airport, army warehouses in Atbara, and fuel depots in Omdurman.

articles.headline: Two militants killed as Colombia steps up air strikes against rebels
articles.summary: Two rebels were killed in air strikes ordered by Colombia’s new government, a military source confirmed. The strike against the National Liberation Army occurred late Monday in the northeastern Catatumbo region, as Bogota pledges to fight violence.

articles.headline: Trump says Secret Service wanted him off the aircraft
articles.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump said the Secret Service and military wanted him on a "different plane" after a trip last month to Turkiye due to a credible threat from Iran. He confirmed a Washington Post report about the subterfuge involved in his flight.

articles.headline: U.S. helicopter fires on ship that tried to break blockade
articles.summary: A U.S. helicopter fired missiles into the engine room of a Panama-flagged cargo ship attempting to break the American blockade of Iran's ports. The M/V Vela Nova was disabled after ignoring warnings, marking the third such forcible halt by the U.S.

articles.headline: Hayden backs India skipper Gill to successfully navigate Test cricket
articles.summary: Matthew Hayden backed Shubman Gill to navigate Test cricket challenges, praising him as a "wonderful young man and a good leader." Hayden stated Gill faces challenges, none more important than Test cricket's survival, and believes he is "up to the challenge."

articles.headline: Italy’s Curtis shatters women’s 50m backstroke world record
articles.summary: Italian teenager Sara Curtis set a new women's 50m backstroke world record of 26.63s in qualifying at the European swimming championships in Paris. She surpassed Australia's Kaylee McKeown previous record of 26.86s set in October 2023.

articles.headline: Kushner, Iger to buy Lakers for record $12.5 billion: report
articles.summary: American businessman Josh Kushner and former Disney executive Bob Iger are reportedly purchasing the LA Lakers for a record-breaking $12.5 billion. They bought controlling interest from Mark Walter, who acquired it for $10 billion in 2025.

articles.headline: Budkowski to drive Cadillac’s fortunes as new team principal
articles.summary: Cadillac replaced team principal Graeme Lowdon with former Alpine director Marcin Budkowski, citing a "planned leadership transition" as the organization moves into its next racing stage. The F1 season resumes with the Dutch GP from August 21-23.

articles.headline: India arrives in the Emerald Isle seeking a fresh path in Tests
articles.summary: India is in Sri Lanka for a two-Test series, starting Saturday, aiming to revive its fortunes in Test cricket. Placed fifth in WTC rankings, Shubman Gill's team faces challenges from retirements, injuries, and selectorial interventions, seeking to overcome transition blues.

articles.headline: Afghanistan set to host India for three T20Is in September
articles.summary: The BCCI and Afghanistan Cricket Board announced a three-match T20I series between India and Afghanistan, to be held in New Delhi from September 13 to 17. This clashes with Bangladesh's hopes of hosting India, and India will serve as Afghanistan's base.

articles.headline: Dickwella replaces injured Kusal Mendis in Sri Lanka squad
articles.summary: Sri Lanka wicketkeeper-batter Kusal Mendis has been ruled out of the two-Test series against India due to injury. Gloveman Niroshan Dickwella, a left-hand batter, makes the 16-member squad for his first Test in over three years.

articles.headline: Anmol and Badoni blaze away in Superstarz’s big win
articles.summary: South Delhi Superstarz secured a nine-wicket victory over East Delhi Riders in the Delhi Premier League, chasing a target of 192 in 16.5 overs. Sanat Sangwan (57), Anmol Sharma (65 n.o.), and skipper Ayush Badoni (66 n.o.) all scored half-centuries.

articles.headline: Indian fencers win three more golds at C’wealth c’ship
articles.summary: The Indian fencing team won three gold, one silver, and one bronze medal on the third day of the Commonwealth Championship in Lagos, Nigeria. Kanaglakshmi, Rajendran Shanthimol Sherjin, and Karan Singh secured gold medals in their respective categories.

articles.headline: Karnataka women get the better of Bihar
articles.summary: Karnataka defeated Bihar 2-1 in a Pool-B match during the Hockey India-junior women National hockey Division ‘B’ championship in Pune on Wednesday. Other results included AP beating Kerala 3-2 and Mizoram beating Assam 6-2.

articles.headline: Indian Army rallies to beat Mohd. Sporting, books quarterfinal berth
articles.summary: Indian Army secured a 2–1 comeback win against Mohammedan Sporting in the Durand Cup, with Shafeel P.P. scoring in stoppage time. This win secured Indian Army's third straight victory and a quarterfinal spot.

articles.headline: EBFC stuns Al Arabi in the 11th hour, seals qualification
articles.summary: East Bengal FC achieved a sensational 4-1 comeback victory in extra time against Kuwait’s Al Arabi SC in the AFC Champions League Two qualifier. Jay Gupta equalised in the 90th minute, then Rashid, Hmar, and Rohit Danu sealed qualification in extra time.

articles.headline: Blame it on injuries and lack of practice for missing the yellow metal at u-20 Worlds, say Indian athletes
articles.summary: Indian athletes, who won three individual medals at the World Athletics U-20 Championships, cited injuries and lack of practice for missing gold. Javelin thrower Ashish Yadav (silver) and high jumper Basant Meghwal (bronze) expressed disappointment, with Shahnavaz Khan (long jump bronze) also battling cramps.

articles.headline: Nadeem decides to skip Lausanne Diamond League
articles.summary: Pakistan's Olympic gold-medallist javelin thrower Arshad Nadeem will skip the Lausanne Diamond League this month to focus on training in South Africa for another international event and the Asian Games in Japan. His coach confirmed he is in rehab.

articles.headline: We want to show the world we can host any event: Sanjay
articles.summary: Badminton Association of India (BAI) general secretary Sanjay Mishra stated India aims to prove its capability to host major international events like the World Championships, Commonwealth Games, and Olympics. This comes after the Indian Open was marred by issues like monkey intrusions and pollution.

articles.headline: Tata Steel World 25K Kolkata on December 20
articles.summary: The Tata Steel World 25K Kolkata, a World Athletics Gold Label race, will take place on December 20. Registrations open Thursday for the 11th edition of the race, which also includes virtual run options across categories.

articles.headline: Moment of reckoning for Gill — the skipper and the batter
articles.summary: Shubman Gill faces his biggest Test captaincy challenges, starting with the Sri Lanka series. With India languishing mid-table in the WTC after a 0-2 loss to South Africa, Gill needs seven wins from nine remaining games to reach the final, amidst squad injuries and his own batting form.

articles.headline: Chandrasekaran to exit Tata Sons chairman post in 2027 amid board rift
articles.summary: Natarajan Chandrasekaran will step down as Tata Sons chairman on February 20, 2027, not seeking a third term after 9 years. His exit follows a reported rift/stalemate with Tata Trusts Chairman Noel Tata over capital allocation, governance, management style, and new business performance/losses (e-commerce, aviation, semiconductors). The announcement led to a ₹45,000 crore drop in Tata Group's market cap. A five-member committee will search for a successor for the conglomerate.

articles.headline: Bank of America acquires 49.9% stake in Jio Credit for $1.9 billion
articles.summary: Bank of America (BoA), via its subsidiary NB Holdings, will acquire a 49.9% stake in Jio Credit (JCL), the lending arm of Jio Financial Services (JFSL), for approximately $1.9 billion (₹18,268 crore). This preferential allotment of equity shares and warrants values Jio Credit at $3.8-$4.4 billion. The deal, Jio Financial’s third global partnership, aims to combine BoA's expertise with Jio's digital reach to expand credit access, retail, and enterprise lending operations in India.

articles.headline: Beant Singh murder convict Hawara declines custody parole
articles.summary: Jagtar Singh Hawara, convicted in the 1995 assassination of former Punjab CM Beant Singh, declined a two-day custody parole from Delhi prisons, seeking regular parole to meet his ailing mother. Punjab CM Bhagwant Mann had requested 10 days' parole on humanitarian grounds for Hawara, who refused custody parole due to heavy police presence.

articles.headline: FCRA Amendment Bill sent to 31-member parliamentary committee
articles.summary: The Lok Sabha referred the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment Bill, 2026, to a 31-member Joint Parliamentary Committee (JPC) following Opposition protests. Opponents claim the bill targets NGOs and minority-run institutions, while Home Minister Amit Shah and Parliamentary Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju deny this, citing a request for review. The JPC is to report by the Winter Session's first week.

articles.headline: India's retail inflation rises to 4.45% in July, exceeding RBI target
articles.summary: India's retail inflation (CPI) rose to 4.45% in July (from 4.38% in June), surpassing RBI's 4% midpoint target for the second consecutive month. Driven by higher food (5.52%) and fuel prices (kitchen staples like onions, ginger, garlic), economists predict continued price pressures due to monsoon impacts, El Niño, and West Asian tensions. While within the 2-6% tolerance, a further rise could prompt RBI rate hikes, though none are immediate.

articles.headline: Delhi's Master Plan 2047 allows Yamuna floodplain construction
articles.summary: The Delhi Development Authority (DDA) approved the Master Plan for Delhi-2047, extending its horizon to align with "Viksit Bharat@2047." The plan reclassifies parts of the Yamuna floodplain (O-Zone) for 'Green Development' and regulated commercial/institutional construction, raising environmentalists' concerns about erosion of buffer zones and increased flooding risks. It also addresses housing, mobility, economic growth, and eases building approvals.

articles.headline: Parliamentary panel finds former Justice Varma guilty of misconduct
articles.summary: A three-member parliamentary inquiry committee found former Delhi/Allahabad High Court Justice Yashwant Varma guilty of three charges, including unexplained Indian currency, failure to preserve evidence after a fire, and evasive explanations. The panel dismissed his defense that cash belonged to his father-in-law. Varma resigned in April, but the findings could lead to impeachment proceedings or affect his post-retirement benefits; further legal action is recommended.

articles.headline: China calls India border situation 'generally stable' amid Tawang face-off
articles.summary: China's foreign ministry stated the border situation with India in the Arunachal Pradesh sector is 'generally stable,' following reports of a brief face-off between Indian and Chinese troops in the Tawang sector. Both nations aim to maintain diplomatic and military communication to prevent misunderstandings and ensure peace along the Line of Actual Control.

articles.headline: Airtel scraps entry-level ₹299 prepaid plan, raising tariffs
articles.summary: Bharti Airtel has discontinued its base-tier ₹299 monthly prepaid plan, effectively raising the entry-level price for users. The minimum monthly recharge is now the ₹349 plan, offering 1.5GB daily data. This move, part of Airtel's strategy to increase Average Revenue Per User (ARPU), is the first major tariff revision in a year.

articles.headline: Tamil Nadu assembly passes resolution against Lok Sabha delimitation
articles.summary: The Tamil Nadu Legislative Assembly passed a resolution urging the Union government to freeze Lok Sabha seats at the current 543 and maintain existing inter-State distribution until 2041. The resolution, supported by DMK and allies, argues that delimitation based on population penalizes states with successful family planning. It also advocates for immediate 33% women's reservation within the current seat count for the 2029 elections.

articles.headline: Kerala HC quashes Centre's FCRA renewal denial for anti-port NGOs
articles.summary: The Kerala High Court set aside a Union Home Ministry order that denied FCRA renewal to two NGOs, Save A Family Plan and Kerala Social Service Forum, which allegedly funded Vizhinjam seaport protests. The court ruled that the constitutional right to peaceful protest cannot be equated with diverting foreign funds for 'undesirable purposes' without proven illegalities, ordering the ministry to reconsider.

articles.headline: Lok Sabha passes bill expanding Centre's power over minerals
articles.summary: The Lok Sabha passed the Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Amendment Bill, 2026, amid Opposition protests. The bill, passed without debate, empowers the Union government to regulate critical minerals and grant exploration licenses directly, while restricting states from levying additional taxes/cesses on mineral rights. This aims to reduce uncertainty and costs in the mineral sector.

articles.headline: Parliament passes bill to officially rename Kerala as 'Keralam'
articles.summary: Parliament has approved a bill to officially change the name of the state of Kerala to 'Keralam' in all official records and the Constitution. The legislation follows a unanimous resolution by the Kerala State Assembly, reflecting the state's traditional Malayalam name and cultural identity. The Union government will implement the renaming across all official documentation.

articles.headline: Defence Ministry issues ₹1 lakh crore tender for 60 transport planes
articles.summary: The Union Defence Ministry has issued a ₹1 lakh crore tender for 60 multirole medium transport aircraft for the Indian Air Force. The project, under 'Make in India' and 'Atmanirbhar Bharat' initiatives, requires the winning global vendor to partner with an Indian company for domestic manufacturing, aiming for high indigenous content. This will replace the aging fleet of Soviet-era An-32 and IL-76 aircraft and boost strategic airlift capabilities.

articles.headline: Fresh violence in Manipur: Nine houses, church burnt in Naga village
articles.summary: Fresh ethnic violence erupted in Manipur's Kangpokpi district as armed miscreants set fire to nine houses and a church in a Naga village. The incident, which saw at least 10 houses and a church ablaze, heightened ethnic tensions. Security forces have been deployed, and tribal bodies called for an immediate investigation and rehabilitation for affected families.

articles.headline: Ukraine strikes Russia's Black Sea naval base in Novorossiysk
articles.summary: Ukrainian forces launched a "unique" nighttime drone and anti-ship missile attack on Russia's Novorossiysk Black Sea naval base, reportedly damaging a major naval vessel, air defenses, piers, and other port infrastructure. Russia claimed to shoot down over 500 drones. The US urged Ukraine to halt strikes on non-Russian oil tankers in the region, fearing oil market destabilization, while Russia warned of retaliation if European countries seize its merchant vessels.

articles.headline: Former Chinese Premier Zhu Rongji, economic architect, dies at 97
articles.summary: Zhu Rongji, former Premier of China and architect of its economic boom, has died at 97. Known as the 'Iron-faced Premier' for his anti-corruption stance and a sharp-tongued reformer, he was pivotal in market-based reforms, transforming state-owned enterprises, reforming the banking system, privatizing housing, and securing China's entry into the WTO in 2001. His policies helped China become the world's second-largest economy but also contributed to issues like excessive debt and trade surpluses.

articles.headline: India withdraws from FIFA ASEAN Cup for Brazil friendly
articles.summary: The All India Football Federation (AIFF) announced India's withdrawal from the FIFA ASEAN Cup, scheduled for October/September, citing a clash with the Indian Super League and other domestic commitments. Instead, the national team will prioritize a high-profile friendly against five-time world champions Brazil on October 3, seeking competitive matches against top-tier global opposition.

articles.headline: Praggnanandhaa beats Sindarov in Sinquefield Cup, shares lead
articles.summary: Indian Grandmaster R. Praggnanandhaa defeated Uzbekistan's Javokhir Sindarov in a 95-move second-round match at the Sinquefield Cup in St. Louis, the penultimate event of the Grand Chess tour. Praggnanandhaa demonstrated superior end-game technique, securing the victory after 63 moves, and is now among five leaders sharing the top spot with 1.5 points.

articles.headline: Sports Ministry suspends TTFI over governance issues, impacts Asiad
articles.summary: The Union Sports Ministry has suspended the recognition of the Table Tennis Federation of India (TTFI) due to persistent governance issues, non-compliance, and failure to conduct timely elections, citing athlete welfare concerns. An ad-hoc committee will manage daily affairs, but the suspension creates uncertainty for India's Asian Games preparations and the fate of foreign expert Massimo Costantini, pending election of a new executive body.

articles.headline: SEBI finds no manipulation in new stock closing auction regime
articles.summary: SEBI Chairperson Madhabi Puri Buch stated no manipulation has been observed in the recently introduced transparent Closing Auction Session (CAS) for stocks, attributing market volatility to trader caution. Sebi aims to boost participation in the mechanism, which determines closing prices based on the final 30 minutes of trading, replacing the previous average practice. Mutual fund participation has increased to 20-25%, up from 5-7%, indicating growing trust.

articles.headline: Tata Motors Q1 net profit jumps 83% on strong CV demand
articles.summary: Tata Motors reported an 83% year-on-year increase in its consolidated net profit for the June quarter, driven by strong volumes and domestic demand in the commercial vehicle (CV) segment, overcoming high fuel prices. Consolidated revenue rose 19% to ₹20,667 crore, with EBITDA up 10% to ₹2,300 crore. The company expects Q2 to improve as supply chain constraints ease and replacement demand remains high.

articles.headline: Grasim Industries Q1 net profit up 39-51%, revenue up 21%
articles.summary: Grasim Industries reported a significant jump in its consolidated net profit for the June quarter: 39% to ₹3,846 crore or 51% to ₹8,077 crore. Consolidated revenue grew 21% to ₹48,716 crore, driven by strong performance in its paints, cement, materials, and financial services businesses. The company also announced a ₹3,157 crore capital expenditure for its standalone business, including rapid expansion of its Birla Opus paint brand to over 1,450 outlets.

articles.headline: Godrej Consumer shares plunge 11% on sudden CEO exit
articles.summary: Godrej Consumer Products shares plunged over 10-11%, marking their steepest daily decline in six years, following the abrupt exit of CEO Sudhir Sitapati, just three months after his reappointment. Finance chief Aasif Malbari was named CEO and MD. This raised concerns about leadership stability, continuity, and the impact on the company's long-term 'Vision 2040' growth strategy and digital transformation plans, alongside existing pressures from high raw material costs and competition.

articles.headline: Apollo Hospitals Q1 net profit jumps 34-38% to ₹581-610 crore
articles.summary: Apollo Hospitals Enterprise reported a 34-38% increase in consolidated net profit to ₹581-610.4 crore for Q1FY27, beating estimates. Revenue grew 15-21% to ₹6,306.9-7,043 crore, driven by robust performance in healthcare services (₹3,619.5 crore), increased surgical volumes, higher occupancy, and its pharmacy/digital health segments. High speciality volumes in cardiology, oncology, neurology, gastroenterology, and orthopaedics also boosted results.

articles.headline: Indian semiconductor startups raise $206 million since 2022
articles.summary: Indian semiconductor startups have raised approximately $206 million across 51 funding rounds since 2022, with $61.9 million in H1 2026 alone. A report highlights increasing investor backing for mature ventures focused on chip design and AI infrastructure, suggesting growing concentration in later-stage startups. Despite the growth, startups need more long-term capital and support for domestic manufacturing to compete globally.

articles.headline: Putin threatens retaliation against EU over Russian ship seizures
articles.summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin threatened the European Union with retaliation if it seizes or sells cargo from Russian commercial vessels, calling such actions 'piracy and banditry.' The commander of Russia's Pacific Fleet confirmed forces are ready to inspect and detain foreign vessels in response to intensifying EU pressure on Russia’s 'shadow fleet,' pledging to respond "in kind."

articles.headline: Overloaded ferry capsizes on Zimbabwe's Lake Kariba, killing 44+
articles.summary: An overloaded government passenger ferry capsized on Lake Kariba in Zimbabwe during rough weather, resulting in at least 44 deaths. The ferry, with a capacity of 90, was carrying at least 114 adult passengers and five crew members; the total number of people on board is unclear due to unticketed children. Search and rescue operations saved 77 individuals, but many remain missing. Survivors reported passengers pleading with the driver to turn back.

articles.headline: Trump administration plans $900 million White House modernization projects
articles.summary: The Trump administration plans to spend at least $900 million on White House 'modernization projects,' diverting funds from various agencies and private donors. This follows a federal appeals court order to halt construction on a $400 million ballroom project. Plans include significant upgrades to the grounds and routine maintenance, without direct Congressional approval for all funds.

articles.headline: Karnataka CM Shivakumar/Siddaramaiah allocates portfolios to 19 new ministers
articles.summary: Ten days after cabinet expansion, CM DK Shivakumar (also referred to as Siddaramaiah in one source) allocated portfolios to 19 new Karnataka ministers. Shivakumar retained finance, law, and Bengaluru planning authorities. Key changes include Ramalinga Reddy moving to Forest and K.H. Muniyappa taking Social Welfare. R.V. Deshpande was appointed Administrative Reforms Commission chief. The move aims to streamline governance ahead of the legislative session.

articles.headline: Amit Shah challenges Opposition to debate NEET protests in Parliament
articles.summary: Home Minister Amit Shah challenged the Opposition to a comprehensive two-day/24-hour debate in Parliament regarding police action during anti-NEET protests and the FCRA Bill, stating the government has nothing to hide. Shah expressed readiness to answer questions, aiming to break legislative deadlock. Opposition leader Rahul Gandhi rejected the offer, demanding answers on who ordered pellet guns on students, not a 'lecture.'

articles.headline: India begins preferential trade talks with Southern African Customs Union
articles.summary: India has signed the terms of reference to launch negotiations for a preferential trade agreement (PTA) in goods with the five-member Southern African Customs Union (SACU), which includes South Africa, Botswana, Namibia, Lesotho, and Eswatini. Both sides aim to conclude talks within one year. This seeks to boost economic ties, increase two-way commerce, and benefit Indian exporters in sectors like automobiles, pharmaceuticals, and industrial machinery, marking India's first major trade pact with an African regional bloc.

articles.headline: Chandrasekaran's exit highlights Tata Sons succession planning gap
articles.summary: N. Chandrasekaran's exit as Tata Sons chairman, amidst a rift over business roadmap and performance, highlights a succession planning gap that Tata Trusts chairman Noel Tata had raised twice. The nomination and remuneration committee had no clear answer, leading to uncertainty as the group faces challenges including a possible market listing, providing an exit for the Shapoorji Pallonji Group, and addressing ballooning losses in new businesses like e-commerce, aviation, and semiconductors.

articles.headline: Tata Group faces new succession test after Chandra's exit
articles.summary: N. Chandrasekaran's decision to step down as Tata Sons chairman exposes a succession-planning gap, an issue Tata Trusts chairman Noel Tata had raised twice. The group faces challenges including a possible market listing, providing an exit for the Shapoorji Pallonji Group, and addressing ballooning losses in new businesses.

articles.headline: Sebi Chairman Pandey defends Closing Auction System amidst market turbulence
articles.summary: Sebi Chairman Tuhin Kanta Pandey defended the newly rolled-out Closing Auction System (CAS), calling it transparent despite initial market turbulence. He acknowledged industry's need for time to understand changes and noted rising mutual fund participation (5-7% to 20-25%). CAS aims to reduce manipulation and tracking error for passive funds, and Sebi has observed no wrongdoing so far.

articles.headline: Ola Electric secures extended battery PLI scheme timeline through 2031
articles.summary: Ola Electric has received approval for revised timelines for its 20 GWh battery-making capacity under the ₹18,100 crore production-linked incentive (PLI) scheme. The Ministry of Heavy Industries (MHI) ensured Ola Electric Mobility receives the full five-year incentive through CY2031, unlocking up to ₹7,240 crore. This transforms the economics of its cell business and extends its battery ambitions.

articles.headline: Yulu raises $93 million in Series C for EV fleet expansion
articles.summary: Yulu, an electric mobility-as-a-service startup, raised $93 million in Series C funding ($63M equity, $30M debt), led by GEF Capital Partners. The funds will quadruple its EV fleet from 50,000 to 200,000 vehicles in two years, expand service hubs, deepen partnerships, and accelerate listing plans, aiming for profitability before an IPO. The capital validates its business model and growth capability.

articles.headline: Tata Group market cap tripled under Chandrasekaran, but recent slowdown
articles.summary: During N. Chandrasekaran's nine-year tenure at Tata Sons, the Tata Group's combined market capitalization more than tripled, net profit rose nearly five-fold, and revenue almost doubled. TCS now accounts for 32% of group valuation, down from 67% five years ago, reflecting diversification. However, his exit follows an earnings slowdown, 3.9% net sales growth in FY26, and a 16.9% market cap decline, underperforming Nifty 50, with unlisted ventures adding to losses.

articles.headline: Uber expands bike and taxi services to 100 new Indian cities
articles.summary: Ride-hailing major Uber is expanding its bike and taxi services to 100 new Indian cities, reaching a total of 225 cities across the country. This expansion, focused on Tier-II and III markets and anchored by Uber Bike, aims to increase its global market presence despite competition from Rapido and Ola.

articles.headline: SBI uses AI to underwrite ₹1 trillion MSME loans in FY26
articles.summary: State Bank of India (SBI) used artificial intelligence (AI) and digital data to underwrite nearly ₹1 trillion in loans to MSMEs in FY26, covering both new and existing customers, with individual loans up to ₹5 crore. The AI-powered Business Rule Engine (BRE) processes GST filings, account info, and credit scores, reducing relationship managers' workload and leading to lower non-performing assets/delinquency in the AI-underwritten portfolio.

articles.headline: Foxconn Q2 profit jumps 35% driven by strong AI demand
articles.summary: Taiwan’s Foxconn, the world’s largest contract electronics maker, reported a 35% rise in second-quarter profit, exceeding analyst forecasts. Strong demand for artificial intelligence (AI) is predicted to drive continued growth this year, with AI-related business, including AI servers, now accounting for 51% of its Q2 revenue.

articles.headline: Karnataka bans tobacco and nicotine products for one year
articles.summary: The Karnataka government, through its Department of Food Safety and Drug Administration, has prohibited the manufacture, storage, sale, and distribution of pan masala and gutkha containing tobacco and nicotine for one year, effective August 10, 2026. The move aims to protect public health and curb the drug menace in the state, with CM Siddaramaiah warning of strict inspections under food safety laws.

articles.headline: Karnataka defers Cauvery water release pending SC hearing
articles.summary: The Cauvery water dispute reignited as the Karnataka government decided to await a Supreme Court hearing outcome before releasing more Cauvery water to Tamil Nadu. The state cabinet discussed the Cauvery Water Management Authority's directive to release 12,000 cusecs, expressing concern over low reservoir storage due to insufficient rainfall and prioritizing local drinking water needs. Tamil Nadu sought SC intervention against Karnataka's non-compliance, impacting basin agriculture.

articles.headline: SC may refer Krishna Janmabhoomi case lead issue to Allahabad HC
articles.summary: The Supreme Court indicated it might remand the Krishna Janmabhoomi-Shahi Idgah Mosque dispute back to the Allahabad High Court to decide which matter should be treated as the lead case. The apex court is considering if the case requires fresh consideration by a single judge, following arguments that the High Court failed to provide adequate notice to all plaintiffs. The hearing was adjourned to September 2.

articles.headline: Air India losses weigh on Chandrasekaran's Tata Sons tenure
articles.summary: Air India has reported approximately ₹47,821 crore in losses since the Tata Group's January 2022 takeover, becoming a major unfinished project for N Chandrasekaran. The transformation faces delays due to supply-chain disruptions, legacy systems, and operational issues, pushing profitability expectations beyond 2032. This challenge, alongside AI's impact on TCS's hiring, marked significant issues as his tenure as Tata Sons chairman concluded.

articles.headline: Delhi HC asks Meta to clarify Rights Manager tool policy
articles.summary: The Delhi High Court has directed Meta to disclose its policy for granting access to its Rights Manager tool, including eligibility criteria and reasons for application rejection. This follows concerns that fraudulent actors misused the tool to file bogus copyright claims against original content creators on Facebook and Instagram, and the court sought clarity amid allegations of exploitation.

articles.headline: West Asia conflict poses fiscal risks for India in FY27
articles.summary: The Finance Ministry informed Parliament's Standing Committee on Finance that the West Asia conflict could impact India's fiscal position in FY27, potentially pushing the fiscal deficit to 5.6% of GDP if crude oil prices reach $130/barrel. The ministry advises strategic energy mitigation and notes states' rising fiscal deficit. The Haryana RERA also extended realty project completion timelines by four months, citing the conflict as force majeure.

articles.headline: Modi advises youth against 'shortcuts,' urges reading autobiographies
articles.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi urged young people in the "era of reels" to avoid 'shortcuts' and read autobiographies for unique historical perspectives, highlighting former president Ram Nath Kovind's life as an example of determination. Speaking at Kovind's autobiography launch, he also noted Kovind's ongoing work on the 'One Nation, One Election' initiative.

articles.headline: Apar Industries, KEI Industries hit new all-time highs on BSE
articles.summary: Apar Industries hit a new all-time high of ~₹18,432 on the BSE, closing at ~₹18,015.0, up 7.6%. Separately, KEI Industries also reached a new all-time high of ~₹5,720, representing a 52% increase over the past year.
